eyebrow: A query that was too broad
code:
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where IPAddress == "{incident_ip}"
| project UserPrincipalName

# {incident_ip} resolved to the corporate VPN's
# shared exit address -- not the attacker's IP
caption: Syntactically correct. The mistake was upstream: what the matched signal actually meant.

steps.label: 38 employees locked out
steps.sub: mid-shift, with no warning, routing through the same VPN exit IP

steps.label: 2 hours of cleanup
steps.sub: the SOC manually re-enabled unrelated accounts, one at a time

steps.label: The real incident
steps.sub: got slower to resolve, not faster

steps.label: Dry-run default
steps.sub: "would disable 39 accounts" is obviously wrong the moment someone reads it

steps.label: Blast-radius cap
steps.sub: one account per action, full stop, regardless of how many the query matches

steps.label: Human approval gate
steps.sub: someone asking "why thirty-nine?" before it executes

caption: Caldera Finance's script skipped exactly this pattern.
